text.p: The following is a direct contribution from commodity statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

White sugar futures in London closed easier in dull, rangebound trade. May lost $0.50 to close at $304.20, while August gave up 0.30 to close at $303.50. There was no fresh news to influence prices. Raw sugar futures in New York closed slightly lower across the board with front month May losing 1 point to close at 10.76 cents/lb, while July shed 3 points to close at 10.52 cents/lb. The market was on the defensive for most of the day with speculators cited as early sellers. Without fresh physical demand, prices could remain under pressure.

RUSSIA - According to official sources sugar imports in January 1997 totalled 90,800 tonnes, tel quel (96,087 tonnes raw value) of which 60,800 tonnes white sugar and 30,000 tonnes raw sugar. Of the total shipments from the Ukraine were 46,800 tonnes, while deliveries from Brazil were 29,200 tonnes, it was said. Total imports in calendar year 1996 reached 3.236 mn tonnes, slightly up on the 1995 figure of 3.186 mn tonnes. Raw sugar imports in 1996 rose to 1.590 mn tonnes from 1.252 mn tonnes the previous year, while white sugar imports fell to 1.546 mn tonnes from 1.934 mn tonnes in 1995.

CANADA - Sugar imports in December 1996 amounted to 205,374 tonnes, raw value, up from last year's 85,861 tonnes. This brought cumulative imports in the first quarter of 1996/97 (October/December) up to 429,416 tonnes, almost 100,000 tonnes up on last year's 329,722 tonnes. Total imports in 1995/96 reached 1.160 mn tonnes against 1.013 mn tonnes in 1994/95. Major countries of origin in October/December 1996 were Australia with 368,996 tonnes raws against 291,062 tonnes and Brazil with 52,578 tonnes compared to nil.

FIJI - According to ISO figures, sugar exports in December 1996 reached 45,129 tonnes, raw value, against nil in the same month the previous year. This brought cumulative imports in the first 8 months of 1996/97 (May/December) up to 447,840 tonnes against 380,450 tonnes in the corresponding period the previous year. Total exports in 1995/96 reached 419,536 tonnes against 498,438 tonnes in 1994/95. Major countries of destination in May/December 1996 were the European Union with 195,896 tonnes raws against 208,420 tonnes, Malaysia with 93,390 tonnes, almost unchanged from last year's 93,308 tonnes and Japan with 80,090 tonnes, up from 32,658 tonnes.

Sugar production in December 1996 amounted to 55,296 tonnes compared to 56,615 tonnes in December 1995. This brought cumulative production in May/December 1996 up to 454,113 tonnes against 453,451 tonnes in the like period the previous year. Total output in 1995/96 amounted to 472,848 tonnes compared to 538,370 tonnes in 1994/95.
